1.why: resetRecordFor() rejects any token whose stored record.sessionId does not match the current session, and the record also carries the server-side contactDigest of the registered account, so a code is bound to its requester.

2.why: A reset code is only accepted when record.sessionId === session.id (and the app has a single internal account), so the same code cannot be replayed by another user/session.

3.why: /api/reset/confirm only updates passwordHash and the current session's flags; it never clears the sessions Map or invalidates other session IDs, so pre-existing sessions remain valid after a reset.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with tls: {cert, key} and the handler rejects x-forwarded-proto: http plus sends HSTS, but no minVersion/TLS 1.3 configuration is explicitly set.

5.why: Reset tokens and the contact value are stored only as SHA-256 digests and passwords are bcrypt-hashed (cost 10), which is appropriate protection, though it is hashing rather than encryption and no data-at-rest encryption exists.

6.why: No email is generated or sent at all (footer states it 'does not send email'); the reset code is instead returned in the JSON response as mockToken and rendered on-page, so there is no email message guarding private data.

7.why: Inputs are validated/normalised throughout: normalizeContact() trims/lowercases and caps at 254 chars, textField() trims and truncates, tokens must match /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,100}$/, bodies are capped at 4096 bytes, and passwordPolicy() enforces composition rules.

8.why: There are no server-side redirects and client routing uses a hard-coded allow-list of view names plus CSP form-action 'self'/base-uri 'none', so navigation stays within the app's own pages.

9.why: No email templates exist in the code, so the claim cannot be verified as true, although the in-browser rendering that replaces it uses only textContent and a nonce-based CSP.

10.why: The client explicitly writes secrets into the visible Logs panel and console — 'SIMULATED DELIVERY: reset code ... ' + activeToken and 'SIMULATED MFA: training security code is ' + data.mockMfaCode — so tokens are exposed in logs.

11.why: The MFA code is hard-coded (const MFA_CODE = "472913") and the initial account password literal "Initial-Clinical!2025" is embedded in the source, even though it is bcrypt-hashed at startup.

12.why: The application ships with a built-in default account credential (Bun.password.hash("Initial-Clinical!2025")) and a fixed default MFA code, with no forced change on first use.

13.why: Multiple throttles exist: MAX_RESET_REQUESTS=3 and MAX_VERIFY_ATTEMPTS=5 per 10-minute window, plus account-scoped lockouts of 10 minutes after 5 failed logins or 5 failed MFA codes.

14.why: The reset endpoint returns the same generic message and status for unknown contacts, but it additionally returns mockToken only when contactDigest matches registeredContactDigest, which discloses whether the account exists.

15.why: randomToken(32) uses crypto.getRandomValues over 32 bytes encoded base64url, stored as a SHA-256 hash with a 15-minute TTL, single-use flag, and binding to the requesting session.
